_note: The single source of truth for repository naming policy. scripts/check_naming.py is the only enforcement point and reads this file; docs/rules/NAMING.md points here and deliberately does NOT restate the table, because a definition copied into a second place is a definition that will be wrong in two places (naming-audit/GLOSSARY.md, 'Scope of counts'). Derived from naming-audit/GLOSSARY.md (PR #423). Change a rule by changing this file, in its own commit, with the audit entry named in `audit_ref`.
_note_statuses: A rule may only be enforced as 'block' when its `status` is in `enforceable_statuses`. This is the load-bearing constraint of the whole file: it makes it impossible to quietly promote an unratified PROPOSAL into something that blocks a merge. Promoting a proposal is a two-key edit (status, then enforcement) and therefore a visible policy change in its own right.
_note_tiers: 'block' fails the gate and blocks a commit or a merge. 'warn' prints [WARNING] and never blocks: those entries are PROPOSED or BLOCKED on an open question in the audit, and the repository owner has not ratified them. 'legitimate' names are recorded so that a later consistency sweep does not 'correct' a term the audit deliberately accepted.

rules.concept: The role that holds a message on behalf of others (store-and-forward custody)
rules.rule: The ROLE is named `node`. `relay` is the VERB for the custody behaviour and must not be used to name the role. Denied terms name a role that the architecture doctrine says does not exist: there are no standalone relays, every node relays.
rules.grandfathered_note: Named in GLOSSARY A-2 as historical identifiers carrying the verb, and as the persisted custody field pair. They are permitted, not endorsed: A-2 proposes no rename for them.
rules.note: `isRelay` is denied on its own terms as well: GLOSSARY A-2's rename plan and FINDINGS F-13 record that its own comment says it no longer distinguishes anything, that it is always false, and that it sits beside `isFull`, which does.

rules.concept: The message as it is stored
rules.rule: One spelling per concept: `MessageRecord` for the stored row, `MessageRecordDto` for any transport shape. The names are FROZEN by a UDL dictionary that both mobile clients bind, so the fix for a competing spelling is to use the frozen one, never to rename it.
rules.note: `StoredMessage` is denied as new vocabulary: GLOSSARY D-4 records that every one of its occurrences sits in wasm/, a crate no CI job builds, and that the type 'does not exist in the build', so adopting it would bind a production name to a phantom type (F-02, F-33). The occurrences that already exist need no grandfather entry because the gate is a line ratchet: it only ever sees lines a change ADDS, so history is never re-litigated.

rules.concept: The encrypted unit on the wire
rules.rule: Three spellings, three distinct meanings, all ACCEPTED-AS-IS: `Envelope` the domain object, `WireEnvelope` its serialized form, `DriftEnvelope` the drift protocol's variant. Denied terms would be a FOURTH spelling of the same thing.
`PeerId` is libp2p's own name for a wire-format identifier and is FROZEN; `identity_id` is serialized and FROZEN. Denied terms are new spellings of an id that the glossary does not own.
rules.grandfathered_note: Explicitly BLOCKED on Q-3 in GLOSSARY A-5. Permitted as-is; renaming them is a decision the owner has not made.

rules.rule: `remove_*` for the domain verb; `forget_*` reserved for ledger-evidence semantics. GLOSSARY B-2 proposes retiring `delete_` outside the UI. NOT ENFORCED: the proposal is unratified, so a new `delete_` warns rather than blocks.

Every binding field carries its unit; `lastSeenMs` is the only inventory name that already does and is the model. A bare `lastSeen` in a binding is the defect. NOT ENFORCED: unratified, and `lastSeenRaw` is BLOCKED on Q-1, which may be a live bug rather than a name.

rules.concept: Competing spellings of the peer-id headword that the audit never measured
rules.rule: `peerID` and `PeerID` occur 67 times across the tree and appear NOWHERE in the audit's measured term list, so the audit has no finding about them. This is recorded as a gap for the owner to rule on, deliberately as 'warn': Swift's own API guidelines prefer `peerID`, so a blanket ban would be wrong, and the audit never decided the question. NOT ENFORCED.

legitimate.why: ACCEPTED-AS-IS in GLOSSARY C-2. A domain term, not a violation.
ACCEPTED-AS-IS in GLOSSARY C-2; it names the behaviour, not a role.
BLOCKED on Q-10, not denied. Permitted until the owner answers.
BLOCKED on Q-11, not denied. D-3 reserves it for the identity broadcast.
A qualified variant of the A-4 trio, not a fourth spelling.
A qualified variant carrying its own meaning; not denied by A-4.
ACCEPTED-AS-IS and named the model to follow.
BLOCKED on Q-1: possibly a live unit bug, not a naming defect.

_note_scope: Scanned extensions: .rs .kt .kts .swift .ts .tsx .js .mjs .py .udl. Exempt prefixes: naming-audit/ (the audit quotes every denied term verbatim), HANDOFF/ and docs/ (prose that discusses the names), tmp/, and generated bindings, whose spellings are owned by the FFI Surface Contract job.
_note_exempt_files: The policy machinery is not subject to the policy it implements. scripts/check_naming.py names every denied term in its self-test, and scripts/measure_uncompiled_counts.py names them because counting them is its job. A gate that flagged its own fixtures would be flagged out of existence on its first commit, and a gate that flags the measuring instrument cannot measure anything.
